correctness.rationale: Theorem 3 in arXiv:2610.09011v1 gives the exact necessity and sufficiency of the radius-four neighborhood inequality. A new exact lex-shadow identity counts disjoint supersets by their lex-earliest selected subset; the block recurrence for its prefix maxima is proved and checked by brute-force neighborhoods in dimensions 6 through 11. The included standalone exact-integer certificate yields maximal violation +329481574 at k=35 and strictly negative maxima for k=36 through 65. Published Theorem 4 supplies all dimensions k>=66. The full claim, its quantifiers and non-systematic setting agree across documents.

value.rationale: The source expressly leaves the exact t>=2 one-redundancy threshold open. Solving kappa_1(2)=36 is a natural structural threshold in coding of function values, is sharp by a concrete 35-bit fiber-size obstruction, and replaces the previous k>=66 guarantee with the exact k>=36 one. A generic exact lex-prefix optimization method avoids astronomical ambient-set enumeration, providing a self-contained finite certificate. This is not a routine tiny parameter increment or a known-table recomputation.
